profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university law school between the lead faculty editor of a transnational legal history symposium issue and the managing editor responsible for source-checking and production logistics. They are preparing a package built around a review essay on Tamar Herzog's Frontiers of Possession, plus a companion note comparing Iberian municipal border disputes with colonial possession claims. The context is that the faculty editor has already spoken informally with the symposium organizer and wants to align handoffs before student editors begin cite-checking. The agenda is to confirm what materials will go into the shared editorial folder, what counts as the 'source packet,' which version of the manuscript should move to cite-check, and what 'clean' and 'final' mean for the next production handoff. The expected outcome is an apparently smooth division of labor: M1 will circulate the packet and substantive guidance, and M2 will launch the editorial workflow for the student team.

members.name: Professor Elena Ruiz
members.role: Faculty Editor for the legal history symposium issue
members.expertise: Early modern Iberian legal history, territorial doctrine, scholarly editing
members.background: A tenured law professor who writes on colonial jurisdiction and has guest-edited prior symposium clusters with minimal administrative intervention.
members.private_state: She wants the issue to move quickly without reopening substantive debates, and she is especially concerned that student editors not flatten the author's nuanced treatment of possession, custom, and shared jurisdiction into modern state-centric language.
hidden_assumptions: When she says the 'source packet,' she means the core authorities students need to verify quotations and major claims, not every archival or historiographic lead mentioned in footnotes.

The 'latest draft' is the version she annotated after the organizer call, even if the file metadata still shows an earlier date because she circulated comments in track changes inside the same document.
A manuscript is 'clean' once substantive edits are settled and only technical cite edits remain, even if track changes and comment bubbles are still visible for the student editors.
The production team will understand that references to the 'Americas section' include only the South America discussion in Herzog, because that is the comparative frame she has been using internally.

members.name: Jordan Patel
members.role: Managing Editor of the law review
members.expertise: Law review production workflow, cite-check coordination, source collection, version control
members.background: A third-year law student who has run source pulls and board transitions for two volumes and relies on standardized editorial processes to keep student teams aligned.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid rework and protect the board from last-minute production surprises, especially incomplete source folders or manuscripts that are not actually ready for cite-check.
hidden_assumptions: A 'source packet' means a complete set of PDFs or scans for every non-readily accessible authority cited in the piece, plus stable links for the rest, because that is what student cite-checkers need to start.
The 'latest draft' means the most recent file in the shared drive with a new filename or timestamp, not a previously named document that has been silently updated.
A document is 'clean' only if all track changes are accepted, comments removed, and Bluebook formatting already normalized enough for line-level cite assignments.

If a faculty editor refers to the 'Americas section,' that naturally includes any discussion of Iberian claims in the New World, including indigenous-title passages and Atlantic framing language across the whole review essay.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the source packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Elena will send over the 'source packet' before student cite-check begins.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this packet will include Herzog, the review essay draft, and a handful of hard-to-access authorities and translated excerpts that anchor the central legal-historical claims.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this packet will include complete sourcing support for the entire manuscript, including all non-obvious secondary works, foreign-language authorities, and materials needed for every footnote assignment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law review settings, 'source packet' is a familiar phrase that sounds standardized, so each assumes the other is using the obvious house meaning without needing to spell out the boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: Which file is the latest draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to moving the 'latest draft' into cite-check after the meeting.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the document she updated after her informal call with the symposium organizer, stored under the same filename with embedded tracked edits and marginal comments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the newest separately saved file in the shared folder, which is an earlier text-only revision that appears more recent by filename convention used by the board.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume there is only one salient current version and the phrase 'latest draft' normally resolves itself in shared-drive practice, so neither thinks to identify the file by exact name.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Jordan can send the piece to the student team once it is 'clean.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'clean' to mean substantively stable, with no expected content rewrites, even if track changes remain visible because they help students follow prior editorial choices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'clean' to mean mechanically clean: all changes accepted, comments deleted, formatting normalized, and ready for assignment without interpretive clutter.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term is routine in editorial conversations and often functions as shorthand for readiness, creating a false sense of precision while masking different readiness criteria.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the student team should pay extra attention to the 'Americas section' because it carries the comparative framing.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes everyone knows this label refers narrowly to the South America portion dealing with Spanish-Portuguese possession disputes and related claims-making practices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this includes all New World framing material in the review essay and companion note, including broader Atlantic references and indigenous-territory discussions wherever they appear.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a straightforward internal label rather than a substantive decision, and both have enough contextual overlap that the broader/narrower distinction never becomes salient during a coordination call.

What I need from Jordan is a smooth handoff: I will give them the core materials necessary to verify the central legal-historical claims, and they can handle the technical side without turning possession and layered jurisdiction into modern sovereignty shorthand.
